name: Lazarus
interpretive_note: Most interpreters read this as a parable, grouped with Jesus's other parables in Luke 15-16, using vivid imagery of Hades rather than literal geography. A minority view notes Jesus never explicitly calls it a parable and it is the only one of His parables to name a character, and reads it as a more literal account of the afterlife. The site does not take a side on this question.
source_summary: The beggar in Jesus's parable of the rich man and Lazarus, who lay at a rich man's gate longing for scraps and was carried after death to Abraham's side, while the unnamed rich man suffered torment and was refused a warning sent back to his living brothers.
family_friendly_summary: Jesus told a story about a poor, sick man named Lazarus who lay outside the gate of a rich man's house, hoping for scraps of food, while the rich man lived in comfort and ignored him. When both men died, Lazarus was carried by angels to be with Abraham in a place of comfort, but the rich man ended up in a place of suffering. The rich man begged for just a drop of water to cool his tongue, but was told it was too late to change things. He then begged for someone to warn his five brothers, but was told they already had God's word to listen to, and that even someone risen from the dead would not convince them if they refused to listen. Jesus's story reminds us that how we treat the poor matters, and that God's word is enough.
adult_story: In one of His parables, Jesus told of two men whose eternal reversal of fortune illustrates the peril of wealth without mercy. A rich man "habitually dressed in purple and fine linen, joyously living in splendor every day," while a poor man named Lazarus lay at his gate, covered with sores, longing to be fed the crumbs that fell from the rich man's table -- even dogs came and licked his sores (Luke 16:19-21). Both men died. Lazarus was carried by angels to Abraham's side, a place of honored rest, while the rich man was buried and found himself in torment in Hades (16:22-23). Seeing Abraham far off with Lazarus, the rich man begged for mercy, asking that Lazarus dip his finger in water to cool his tongue, but Abraham explained that their situations, reversed from life, were now fixed by an uncrossable chasm (16:24-26). The rich man then begged that Lazarus be sent to warn his five living brothers, but Abraham answered that they already had Moses and the Prophets to listen to (16:27-29). When the rich man insisted a messenger from the dead would surely persuade them, Abraham gave the parable's haunting final line: "If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead" (16:31). Lazarus is the only character Jesus ever names within one of His parables.
devotionals: Jesus's parable carried Lazarus the beggar to Abraham's side after a life this world ignored. Jesus welcomes us, however overlooked, into His lasting comfort.
The rich man begged for a warning sent from the dead, but Abraham pointed to Moses and the Prophets. May we trust Jesus's word already given to us.
